name: Executive order of August 31, 1876 adding land to the Gila River Reservation for the Pima and Maricopa
citation: Executive order of August 31, 1876 (1 Kappler 806; Royce area 596)
nations: Akimel O'odham (Pima) and Piipaash (Maricopa), today the Gila River Indian Community and the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community
promises: Not a treaty: a presidential order. It set apart listed sections in Townships 4 and 5 South, Ranges 7 and 8 East, as an addition to the Gila River Reservation that Congress established on February 28, 1859 (Royce p. 888, area 596).

The Indian Claims Commission found this order and the order of June 14, 1879 reserved further parts of Pima-Maricopa aboriginal land to protect their farms from white settlers (Docket 228, additional finding 26).
landTaken: None taken by this order; it added land to the reservation.
today: In Docket 228 the Indian Claims Commission found the growth of the Pima reservations between 1859 and 1883 inconsistent with an intent to take their aboriginal title, and fixed the taking of Pima-Maricopa aboriginal land not already entered by settlers at November 15, 1883, the date of a later order (opinion and interlocutory order of January 20, 1972). Congress later set conditions on the plan for the Docket 228 judgment funds (Public Law 108-22, 2003).

nationVoice.summary: Its timeline says the 1876 addition of about 9,000 acres around Blackwater only reserved land the Akimel O'odham already occupied and did nothing to solve the loss of their water.

The Community says Congress set apart the first reservation in Arizona for it in 1859, and that in the 1870s and 1880s upstream diversions and dams built by non-Native farmers cut off its Gila River water and largely wiped out its farming, followed by decades of famine.

openQuestions: treaties.json error: presentDayTribes is empty for this record; the Gila River Indian Community (and, for the Pima and Maricopa generally, the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community) should be listed. Not edited.

Royce refers this entry to the orders of January 10, June 14, 1879 and May 5, 1882; whether any part of the 1876 addition was later cut was not established, and under the rule for executive-order land a later cut would not be a breach by itself.
The Gila River water claims (Docket 236 series) concern the loss of water, not this order; they were not traced for this file.
The order was read in Royce's summary and in the Commission's citation (1 Kappler 806), not in Kappler itself.
